summary: 37 units reviewed. 15 issues of severity error, 15 minor (applied patches validated against chunk2_out.json). Damaged-print units: 45 (invented padma/ca/āhva split and 'lotus (?)' removed, translations hedged), 56 (conjectured measures were stated as the text), 68 (damaged compound was silently altered and translated plainly, Hindi added 'made from'); all three keep confidence low. glossary_suggestions.suggest: When the printed form is trivṛtā (nominative of the ā-stem, used throughout this chapter as the drug name), set `w` to 'trivṛtā' with 'f. nom. sg.'; use 'trivṛt' only for the t-stem forms (e.g. unit 38 'trivṛt'). Drafts in chunk 2 wrote 'trivṛt' for 'trivṛtā' (units 42, 46, 48, 55).
Hindi: keep यव (not जौ), per the no-plant-common-names rule. English: OPEN, 'barley' is a plant identification; either 'yava (a grain)' or accept 'barley grains' book-wide.

Glosses differ between units (vyoṣa 'a set of three drugs', tryūṣaṇa 'a set of three pungent drugs'). Use 'a set of three pungent drugs' for vyoṣa and tryūṣaṇa, 'a set of three fruits' for triphalā, 'a set of three' for trijātaka.
One rendering in English and Hindi: 'unctuous' / स्निग्ध (unit 51 'unctuous (oiled)', unit 66 'greased'/चिकने).

Convention for printed words that cannot be restored: keep the printed form as one unsplit `w`, gloss 'unclear (printed word not restored)', gram 'unclear'; in English and Hindi write 'on a conjectural reading of damaged print' (अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार), quote the printed words, give no ingredient or measure as fact; confidence low. No brackets or Latin letters in Hindi.
